opt.cpu_idle.title: Let the CPU slow down when idle
opt.cpu_idle.desc: The current power plan keeps the CPU at full speed even when idle, producing constant heat. After this change the CPU slows down when idle; performance under load is unchanged.
opt.cpu_boost.title: Allow CPU turbo boost
opt.cpu_boost.desc: The current power plan disables turbo boost, so the CPU never runs above its base clock, even under load. After this change turbo works the Windows default way again; the CPU still slows down when idle.
apps.add.title: Choose a preference for {0}
apps.hint: Choose how apps are scheduled. Apps without a setting use Automatic
pref.auto.desc: Yields when it keeps the processor busy in the background; apps in use or used recently are left alone
pref.always_fast.desc: Never yields performance and is never throttled by Windows
pref.background.desc: Always runs on efficiency cores at lower priority
pref.game.desc: Runs one priority level higher and is never throttled by Windows; switches to the mode chosen for games and uses the dedicated GPU
remedy.none: Cannot be handled separately; resets after a restart
since_boot.title: Compared with startup
since_boot.caption: Up for {0} · Baseline recorded {1}
since_boot.pending: A baseline is recorded about 5 minutes after startup. Changes in system totals appear here afterwards.
since_boot.note: Items marked in orange have grown well beyond normal use. The system cache holds file data that Windows releases automatically when programs need memory, so it is not cleaned.
settings.tray_alert.desc: Show a dot on the tray icon for high temperature, high memory usage and similar conditions
hw.cpu.hybrid: {0} performance cores ({1} threads) + {2} efficiency cores ({3} threads)
apps.smart_schedule.desc: Apps that keep the processor busy in the background move to efficiency cores at lower priority, so the apps you use are not disturbed; games and apps playing sound are never throttled by Windows. Turning it off restores every app
apps.system.desc: Resident system and driver programs, shown for reference. Poise does not adjust system programs
apps.not_running.desc: Apps that have a category or have run before; the category applies the next time they run

updater.title: Poise Update
updater.installing.detail: Allow the installation when Windows asks. Poise closes briefly while it installs; your system settings stay as they are.
updater.done.detail: Poise is running again. Its icon is in the taskbar.
updater.up_to_date.detail: There is no newer version to install.
updater.failed.network: Couldn't reach GitHub, or the download was interrupted. Check your connection and try again from Settings.
updater.failed.verification: The downloaded installer failed verification and was deleted. Try again later from Settings.
updater.failed.declined: Administrator permission wasn't granted, so Poise stays on its current version.
updater.failed.launch: The installer didn't start (security software may have blocked it), so Poise stays on its current version.
updater.failed.install: The installation didn't finish (code {0}). The previous version has been restored.
updater.failed.start: The new version is installed, but the Poise service didn't start. Try restarting your PC.
updater.failed.unfinished: The installer didn't finish in time, so it's unclear whether the new version was installed. Restart your PC and check the version in Settings.
home.cores.desc: Core groups, caches and load, and which cores programs run on
home.activity.desc: What Poise adjusted and why, and a record of each game or heavy task
span.hybrid.main_plus: the big cores and {0} small-core group(s)
span.groups.main_plus: the main core group and {0} more group(s)
cores.title: Cores and cache
cores.summary.hybrid: {0} big cores, {1} small cores, {2} threads in {3} groups
cores.demand.high: CPU demand: high (a focus program is running or the CPU has no headroom; background programs fully yield)
cores.demand.normal: CPU demand: normal (the program in use is busy; background programs run at lower priority)
cores.demand.none: CPU demand: none (background programs don't need to yield)
cores.note.off: Smart scheduling is off: Poise doesn't place programs, and Windows schedules all of them.
cores.note.single: All cores on this processor share one cache, so Poise doesn't restrict which cores programs use. It only adjusts priorities.
cores.cache_note: Windows doesn't report how much cache each program uses. Each core group shares an L2 cache, so programs placed in the same group share it; a program restricted to one group only uses that group's cache.
cores.programs.none: No programs are restricted to this group
cores.unrestricted.desc: The busiest programs without a core restriction; they can run on any core
activity.title: Log and records
log.demand.high: CPU demand is now high: background programs fully yield
log.demand.normal: CPU demand is now normal: background programs run at lower priority
log.demand.reason.in_use: The program in use is busy
log.demand.none: CPU demand is now none: background programs don't need to yield
log.what.yielded: busy in the background, yielded (small cores, lower priority, efficiency mode)
log.what.lowered: busy in the background, lower priority (still uses idle cores)
log.what.not_playing: no longer scheduled as a game
log.cause.marked: Set to always fast or game
log.moved_aside: {0} idle programs moved to the small cores, keeping the big cores for the focus program
log.moved_aside.groups: {0} idle programs moved to other core groups, keeping the main group for the focus program
log.moved_back: No focus program anymore; moved programs can use all cores again
log.access_denied.desc: A protected program (for example, a game with anti-cheat); Poise won't try again
log.recovered: Poise didn't exit cleanly last time; restored {0} programs that were still running
log.recovered.desc: {0} processes were adjusted at the time
log.throttled: The CPU is being throttled (thermal or power limit reached)
log.unthrottled: The CPU is no longer throttled
log.plan_switched: The power plan changed; the current mode was written to the new plan
log.setting_restored: Another program changed {0} to {1}; changed back to {2}
log.reapplied: The optimization "{0}" was undone; applied it again
log.efficiency_slider: The Windows power mode is set to Best power efficiency
log.efficiency_slider.desc: It overrides some power plan settings, so Poise's modes only partly take effect
log.observe_only: Observe mode: decisions only, no changes
log.paused: Poise exited; process adjustments, cooling and power plan were all restored
log.smart_off: Smart scheduling turned off; process adjustments were undone
records.empty: No usage records yet. When a game or a program that keeps the CPU busy runs, Poise records that time.
records.moved: {0} programs moved to the small cores, {1} background programs yielded
records.moved.groups: {0} programs moved to other core groups, {1} background programs yielded
